question: Voriconazole is the first-line antifungal agent for invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in immunocompromised patients.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Voriconazole is indeed first-line for invasive aspergillosis. It replaced amphotericin B as the standard of care following a landmark trial (Herbrecht 2002, NEJM) showing better survival and fewer adverse effects. Monitoring for hepatotoxicity and visual disturbances is required.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Voriconazole is the standard of care for invasive aspergillosis (IDSA/ECMM guidelines) due to superior survival benefit over amphotericin B demonstrated in landmark RCTs. Alternatives include isavuconazole (similar efficacy, better tolerability) and liposomal amphotericin B. Galactomannan antigen assay (serum or BAL) is the key diagnostic biomarker.
